title: Glucose-activity coupling shifts with diabetes severity
statement: Glucose-activity rank correlation becomes less negative (towards zero) with increasing diabetes severity, reflecting impaired metabolic responsiveness to physical activity.
mechanism: In healthy individuals, physical activity draws down blood glucose through insulin-independent GLUT4 translocation and increased metabolic demand, producing a negative glucose-activity correlation. As diabetes progresses, insulin resistance and impaired glucose uptake in skeletal muscle reduce the glucose-lowering effect of activity, weakening the negative correlation. In advanced disease, counter-regulatory hormone excess may even produce paradoxical glucose responses to activity.
predictions: Glucose-activity Spearman correlation is negative in healthy controls and shifts towards zero across severity groups
The trend is monotonic across healthy -> pre-diabetes -> oral medication -> insulin-dependent
The shift survives adjustment for HbA1c, BMI, and raw glucose/activity levels

literature.title: Network physiology reveals relations between network topology and physiological function
literature.key_finding: Inter-organ coupling structure changes with physiological state.
literature.relevance: Framework for quantifying glucose-activity coupling as a physiological network edge.

key_challenges: Activity measurement noise from wrist accelerometry
Confounding by meal timing relative to activity bouts
dataset_limitations: No meal timing annotations to separate activity-driven vs meal-driven glucose changes

test_plan.primary_method: Kruskal-Wallis test with Jonckheere-Terpstra trend test and FDR correction
implementation_steps: Compute per-person Spearman correlation between glucose and activity on aligned 5-min grid
Test for group differences across diabetes severity
Run sensitivity analyses adjusting for HbA1c, BMI, and raw levels
test_plan.success_criterion: FDR-significant shift of glucose-activity correlation towards zero with increasing severity
test_plan.refutation_criterion: No significant group difference or reversal of expected direction
sensitivity_checks: Full confounder adjustment including raw levels

results.method_used: Kruskal-Wallis with FDR correction, Cohen's d for ordered contrast

sensitivity_checks.name: Full adjustment (HbA1c, BMI, raw levels)
sensitivity_checks.details: FDR=8.22e-07 after full adjustment — effect survives but attenuated

results.interpretation: Glucose-activity coupling becomes less negative with increasing diabetes severity, consistent with impaired metabolic responsiveness to physical activity. The effect is robust even after full confounder adjustment (FDR=8.22e-07), though attenuated, indicating the coupling shift carries information beyond raw HbA1c and BMI.

issues: Group-level median values not recorded in detail
confounders_missed: Medication effects on glucose response to exercise
suggestions: Attempt event-triggered analysis around exercise bouts

notes: Complementary to H-MIG01 (glucose-HR coupling). Together they show that multiple coupling edges shift with diabetes severity.
